title: Client Companies (Slots)
markdown:
The **clients** module (`openexecutive.clients`) adds **multi-client mode** for fractional executives: one Open Executive instance serving several client companies, exactly **one active at a time**. It generalizes the fixture switcher's swap machinery into named, durable *slots* — save files of the full company context. Single-company installs are untouched: nothing changes until a slot is explicitly created, and the `/clients` page shows only an intro until then.

## What a slot contains

Each slot lives at `company/_client_slots/<slug>/` (gitignored — client data is never committable):

| Artifact | What it carries |
| --- | --- |
| `state.db` | A transactionally-consistent copy of the shared SQLite DB — chat history, scheduled actions, onboarding plans, talent pipeline, departments, people, watchlist, audit/run history |
| `profile.yaml` | The company profile |
| `docs/`, `skills/` | Company documents (all file types) and company-authored skills |
| `mcp_servers.json` | Per-client external MCP tools (e.g. one client's Crayon or Google Workspace credentials) |
| `meta.json` | Display name + created/saved timestamps |

## Switching

`POST /clients/{slug}/activate` saves the current client back to its slot (`VACUUM INTO` for the DB copy), then restores the target: the DB through sqlite3's online **backup API** (the live file's inode never changes, so handles held elsewhere stay valid), the company artifacts by replacement, and the ChromaDB `company_docs` collection + company skills re-indexed from the restored directories. Idempotent schema initializers re-run after every restore, so a slot saved before a schema-adding deploy gains the new tables. Activating a **blank** slot (created with `source: "blank"`, no `state.db` yet) factory-wipes the per-client tables and re-seeds defaults — departments, onboarding templates, principal briefs, cadences — so the new client's Today page works without a restart.

The first activation from single-company mode auto-snapshots the original company to `_user_backup` (the same restore point the fixture switcher uses); `POST /fixtures/unload` brings it back and exits client mode.

## Invariants

- At most one slot is active — recorded in an allowlist-validated `.active_client` sentinel.
- **Only the active client is live**: its scheduled actions fire, its docs are indexed; parked clients sleep. The single-instance scheduler constraint is unchanged.
- Slot operations share the fixture switcher's destructive-op lock, so fixture loads, snapshots, resets, and slot switches serialize against each other. The Notion sync tick coordinates with the same lock without queueing on it: it skips its tick while the lock is held, fetches from Notion unlocked, and takes the lock only for its short local write phase — aborting without writing if the active client changed mid-fetch (in-process only; a CLI run is a separate process the lock cannot see). The Outline sync tick follows the identical pattern. A fixture and a client are never active simultaneously (slot ops refuse with 409 while a fixture is loaded); loading a fixture saves an active client back to its slot first, so demos can never destroy client work. Factory reset clears the active-client sentinel but preserves slot directories.
- `generated_fixtures` is operator-level (the demo library) and is preserved verbatim across switches.
- Each client gets a stable Honcho workspace (`openexec-client-<slug>`) so peer memory survives parking; fixture teardown paths recognise the prefix and never delete these.

## Caveats

`mcp_servers.json` is read by the MCP gateway at process startup — a switch that changes it takes effect on the next API restart (the activate response carries `mcp_config_changed`). Scheduled actions whose `run_at` passed while a client was parked are claimed on the first tick after activation; authority gates still apply, but expect the returning client's overdue follow-ups to fire shortly after a switch.

## Setting up a new engagement with AI

`POST /clients/generate` turns **real intake material** into a reviewable draft of the client: profile, org, roster, starter docs, and known history. Intake material is pasted text (kickoff-call notes, a brief, website copy) and/or **file attachments** (PDF, Word, Excel, CSV, Markdown/text; the request is multipart). Each attachment's extracted text both feeds the draft and is appended to the bundle as a `source_<name>.md` company doc, so it lands in the seed slot and is indexed into the `company_docs` collection on activation alongside the AI-written docs (extracted text, not the original binary; legacy `.xls` is unsupported). It runs the Council-configurable `engagement_intake` agent — the grounded sibling of the demo fixture generator (same bundle schema, validation, and repair-retry; the Company Simulator's fictional path is unchanged). Grounding rules: extract, don't invent — unstated numbers stay null, only people named in the material appear, docs are engagement working documents (intake brief, current-state summary, stakeholder map, open questions), and **no contact handles are ever imported**, even if present in the notes.

Saving the reviewed draft (`POST /clients` with `source: "generated"`) writes a **seed slot**: profile and docs as normal slot artifacts, plus `people.yaml` / `departments.yaml` / `memory.json` in the same shapes curated fixtures use. Nothing touches live state until activation, when the blank-restore path applies the seed files with the fixture loader's seeders and skips the default-department reseed (the draft supplied the org). After the first save-back writes `state.db`, the seed files remain as the engagement's birth record but are no longer consulted; `meta.json` records `origin: "generated"` and the intake notes.

## The practice layer: engagement metadata + cockpit

Each slot's `meta.json` carries optional **engagement metadata** — your role for the client, engagement status (active/paused/winding down/completed), start and renewal dates, retainer (display only), and primary contact — editable via `PATCH /clients/{slug}` for active *and* parked slots, because meta.json lives outside the swapped client state. Renewal awareness deliberately lives here and never as scheduled actions (those swap with the client and would vanish when parked).

The **practice cockpit** (`GET /clients/cockpit`) gives cross-client awareness without touching the one-active-client ceiling: the active client is counted from the live DB, and each parked client's `state.db` is opened **read-only, in place** — no activation, no lock. Cards roll up pending/overdue follow-ups, awaiting replies, unread alerts, onboarding tasks due within a week, and renewal countdowns. Parked data is as fresh as the slot's last save point and every card says so; one broken slot degrades to a single error-flagged card, never a failed board. Cockpit cards link to the **engagement value report** — a workflow that turns the client's own record (decisions, deliverables, follow-through) into a renewal-ready artifact, reading parked clients without activating them. With two or more clients, `/today` gains an "Across your clients" section for the parked ones — single-company installs see none of this, anywhere.

## Overnight rotation (cockpit v2)

With `CLIENT_ROTATION_ENABLED=true` (off by default), a nightly scheduled job (`CLIENT_ROTATION_TIME`, default 03:30 UTC) activates each parked client in turn, generates its morning brief as an artifact in that client's own record, runs its monitor scan, saves it back, and **always restores the original active client** — then delivers one cross-client digest via the original client's principal channel. Two safety rails matter: the scheduler **pauses claiming** while the rotation's `.rotation_in_progress` marker exists (so a just-activated client's overdue outbound backlog can never fire at 3am — rotation does brief + monitors only, never outbound), and the rotation row is re-seeded after every slot activation because scheduled rows swap with the client. Completed engagements and never-activated slots sleep through rotation; per-client failures are skipped and reported in the digest.

## API + UI

`GET /clients` (list + active + fixture status), `POST /clients` (`source: "current"` captures the live company and activates; `"blank"` creates an empty client to onboard fresh; `"generated"` saves a reviewed intake draft as a seed slot), `POST /clients/generate` (grounded AI draft from intake notes and/or file attachments; multipart), `PATCH /clients/{slug}` (engagement metadata), `GET /clients/cockpit` (practice board), `POST /clients/save` (checkpoint without switching), `POST /clients/{slug}/activate`, `DELETE /clients/{slug}` (refuses the active slot). The `/clients` page lives under Settings → advanced tools.
